episode.title: Honor server retry advice without restarting its countdown
episode.before: At parent commit ab021e9f137c9daacf6ae06a495f3c7d6199fab2, the HTTP retry loop ignored Retry-After and always slept for locally computed backoff. Higher-level errors stored an optional relative Duration, so time spent transporting, mapping, reporting, or exhausting a retry could effectively restart the server-advised wait.
episode.after: At commit 9d8de196748b57d7f463a7757eaa447b6483a331, Retry-After delay-seconds and HTTP-date values are captured as a monotonic deadline when advice is received. That deadline is carried through transport, API, protocol, provider-specific, stream-retry, and exhausted-retry error paths. HTTP and stream retries sleep until the original deadline, use local backoff only when advice is absent, and retain expired advice as an explicit zero remaining delay.
episode.diff: Introduced the RetryAfter deadline value and header parser; attached it to HTTP transport errors; replaced relative retry-delay fields with deadline-bearing advice across API and protocol errors; preserved it during generic and provider-specific error mapping; changed HTTP and response-stream retry scheduling to sleep until the captured deadline; retained the deadline in exhausted response-retry state; and added unit and integration tests for parsing, countdown, expiry, propagation, delayed notification, ordinary response retries, and remote compaction retries.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit identifies the defect as HTTP retries using local backoff despite Retry-After and relative delays failing to account for propagation or reporting time; it states that the fix parses advice into a monotonic deadline and preserves it through retry paths.

RetryAfter represents the earliest advised follow-up time as a Tokio Instant, parses nonnegative delay seconds or HTTP dates, exposes the original deadline, and saturates expired remaining delay to zero.
Before the change, the HTTP retry loop contained an explicit TODO to respect Retry-After, always computed local backoff, and slept for that relative duration.
The HTTP transport captures Retry-After from response headers before consuming the body and stores the resulting advice on non-success TransportError::Http values.
The HTTP retry loop now uses the captured advice when present, records its remaining delay, and sleeps until its original deadline; local backoff remains the fallback only when advice is absent.

The protocol error representation changed from an optional relative Duration to an optional RetryAfter deadline; remaining server delay is derived at observation time, and expired advice remains Some(Duration::ZERO).

API-to-protocol error mapping extracts retry advice before changing error details and reapplies the same RetryAfter value to the mapped error, including retryable, rate-limit, overload, and HTTP transport errors.
Provider-specific expired-signature remapping preserves the original retry deadline while replacing the user-facing error details.

Response-stream retry handling reads the preserved deadline, performs notification work, recomputes the remaining telemetry delay, sleeps until the original deadline, and stores that deadline when retries are exhausted.
Parser tests verify delay-seconds countdown, HTTP-date handling, explicit zero and expired dates as valid zero-delay advice, and rejection of malformed or overflowing values.
A paused-time stream test delays retry notification and verifies that the retry resumes at the original server deadline rather than waiting the full relative duration after notification completes.
An exhausted-HTTP-retry test verifies that the last captured deadline survives API error mapping, counts down across elapsed time, and remains present with zero remaining delay after expiry.

End-to-end response retry coverage returns a 503 with Retry-After: 1, verifies HTTP-layer retry telemetry, waits at least the advised interval, completes successfully, and observes exactly two requests.
Remote compaction coverage verifies that a 503 carrying Retry-After is retried at the HTTP layer after the advised interval and that compaction completes through the subsequent successful response.
A provider-specific test verifies that rewriting an expired-signature error retains the exact RetryAfter value.

candidate_atomics.name: capture-server-retry-deadline
candidate_atomics.description: Normalize server retry advice into one monotonic deadline at the point where the advice is received.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent elapsed processing time or wall-clock changes from restarting or corrupting a server-advised retry interval.
semantic_action.pre_state: A failed response or streamed error supplies retry advice as delay seconds, an HTTP date, or a parsed relative delay.
semantic_action.post_state: Valid advice is represented by one monotonic deadline captured at receipt; expired or explicit-zero advice remains valid with zero remaining delay, while invalid advice is absent.
semantic_action.validation: Paused-time parser tests verify countdown and expiry; date and malformed-value cases verify accepted and rejected input forms.

candidate_atomics.name: preserve-retry-deadline-across-error-transforms
candidate_atomics.description: Carry the original deadline through error classification, wrapping, provider adaptation, and exhausted-retry state without converting it back to a fresh duration.

semantic_action.intent: Keep retry timing semantics intact while errors cross abstraction boundaries or receive new user-facing details.
semantic_action.pre_state: An error contains a captured server retry deadline and must be mapped, wrapped, reclassified, or retained after retry exhaustion.
semantic_action.post_state: The transformed error or recovery state contains the same original deadline; querying remaining delay reflects elapsed time and returns zero after expiry instead of losing the advice.
semantic_action.validation: Exhausted-retry mapping and provider-specific remapping tests assert deadline identity, countdown, and post-expiry preservation.

candidate_atomics.name: schedule-http-retry-at-server-deadline
candidate_atomics.description: Prefer the captured server deadline for retryable HTTP failures and use local backoff only when valid advice is absent.

semantic_action.intent: Honor server load-control timing while retaining recovery for responses that provide no valid retry advice.
semantic_action.pre_state: A retry policy admits another HTTP attempt after a retryable failure, with either captured server advice or no advice.
semantic_action.post_state: With advice, the next request is delayed until the original server deadline; without advice, the configured local backoff determines the delay.
semantic_action.validation: Response and remote-compaction integration tests inject Retry-After on an overload response, observe HTTP retry telemetry, verify the advised wait, and confirm successful subsequent requests.

candidate_atomics.name: schedule-stream-retry-with-elapsed-work-accounted
candidate_atomics.description: Use the original deadline after retry reporting or other asynchronous work, and retain it when stream retries are exhausted.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure notification, error propagation, and recovery bookkeeping consume part of the server-advised wait instead of postponing recovery by a new full interval.
semantic_action.pre_state: A retryable stream error carries a server deadline, and recovery may perform asynchronous reporting or reach its retry limit before resuming or returning the error.
semantic_action.post_state: An admitted retry sleeps only until the original deadline, while an exhausted retry records and returns that same deadline for later recovery decisions.
semantic_action.validation: A virtual-time test blocks retry notification and proves resumption occurs at the original deadline; exhausted-retry coverage proves the deadline survives subsequent error mapping and expiry.

candidate_workflows.name: preserve-and-honor-server-retry-timing
candidate_workflows.description: Resolve retry-timing drift by capturing server advice once, preserving its deadline across every error boundary, and making HTTP and stream recovery schedule against that deadline while retaining local fallback only for absent advice.

workflow_graph.goal: Make all relevant retry paths honor one server-defined earliest retry instant without restarting the countdown during error propagation or reporting.
workflow_graph.entry_state: Retryable HTTP or streaming failures may contain server advice, but HTTP retries use local backoff and higher layers represent advice as a relative duration that can be restarted after elapsed processing.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Valid advice is captured once as a monotonic deadline, survives all applicable error transformations and exhausted states, drives HTTP and stream retry timing, and remains distinguishable from absent advice after expiry.
unresolved_or_deferred: The implementation leaves a TODO for preserving retry advice when reading an unbounded error body itself fails without reclassifying that failure as an HTTP-status error.
The bundle does not include PR reviews or status-check results, so validation is grounded in committed test code rather than external CI evidence.

unresolved_questions: The GitHub bundle lacks the issue/PR body, comments, reviews, timeline, and status checks.
The checkout was inspected statically at the pinned commit; no test execution result was supplied by the evidence bundle.

The workflow edge from HTTP scheduling to stream scheduling reflects the observed layered recovery path, but HTTP-only and stream-originated advice can exercise the two scheduler actions independently.
